summary: Full backend + frontend regression for SKL Enterprises CRM. Wrote pytest suite covering auth, brute-force, all 3 public submissions (contact, agent, career+resume upload), admin CRUD (list/search/filter/sort, status update, notes, CSV export, resume download, auth guards). Verified UI end-to-end via Playwright: home loads, contact/agent/career forms submit successfully (toasts + DB persisted rows confirmed), admin login/logout/tab switching/search/status change/notes/CSV export/resume view/protected-route redirect all work.

minor.issue: Brute-force lockout is keyed on request.client.host+email. Behind the K8s ingress, request.client.host is the internal pod-source IP which varies per pod (observed 10.49.136.2 and 10.49.136.6), so an attacker gets 5 attempts per pod (~5 * N_pods) before lockout. Use X-Forwarded-For (first entry) or key the lockout on email-only for stronger protection.
Endpoint accepts any email string (uses str, not EmailStr). Minor: no validation on malformed email.
When collection is empty the code substitutes `docs=[{}]` producing a CSV with one empty row instead of just headers. Cosmetic.

ui_bugs.issue: data-testid naming inconsistency: form inputs are 'contact-name', 'contact-email-input', 'contact-phone-input' while the contact info cards use 'contact-email' / 'contact-phone' for mailto/tel links. The review_request lists 'contact-name' as if the same pattern applied. Rename form inputs to 'contact-email' / 'contact-phone' (and rename the info-card links to 'contact-info-email' etc.) for consistency and to match the referenced spec.

action_items: Harden brute-force lockout key (use X-Forwarded-For or email-only) so multi-pod deployments enforce the intended 5-attempt limit.
Align contact form data-testids with the spec (contact-name / contact-email / contact-phone / contact-subject / contact-message / contact-submit). Rename mailto/tel card testids to avoid collision.
Use EmailStr in /api/careers Form to reject malformed emails.
Optional: return only headers (no phantom empty row) when exporting an empty collection.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py hardcodes lockout identifier from request.client.host — behind ingress this is not the client IP; use the X-Forwarded-For chain.
AdminDashboard.viewResume passes the JWT via URL query string (?auth=<token>) which is logged in server access logs / browser history. Consider POST + blob download or short-lived signed URL.
server.py currently has no rate limit on public POST endpoints (/api/contact, /api/agents, /api/careers); consider basic per-IP throttling to prevent spam/abuse.
seed_data_creation: Created contacts/agents/careers rows prefixed with UI_TEST_ or TEST_ during testing; a career record with resume ui_test_resume.pdf was persisted. Test rows for admin status/notes flow are set to Rejected after runs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test suite at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py is self-seeding (each admin test creates its own contact/career via public endpoints, so it works with pytest-xdist loadscope). Only known runtime quirk: brute-force lockout requires ~6–10 attempts to trigger because backend runs on multiple pods; the test does 8 attempts and passes. No mocks. Resume upload uses Emergent object storage (real). Emails via Emergent Resend integration are best-effort (non-blocking).
rca_of_the_issue: Brute-force lockout gap: identifier = f"{request.client.host}:{email}". Behind Kubernetes ingress the framework observes the internal L7 proxy IP which round-robins per pod, so each pod maintains an independent counter in the shared Mongo collection. Fix: derive client IP from request.headers['x-forwarded-for'].split(',')[0].strip() (with a safe fallback), or key the lockout on email alone.
